decision_sentences_latex: The pre-registered rule of \ref{app:lora_question} reads: ``A sign-flip on either contrast, or a magnitude reduction by more than half of the original effect, would be evidence that the frozen-encoder result is encoder-state-specific and would limit the generalisation claim of Contribution~3.'' On LoRA-UNI features (Table~\ref{tab:lora_planned_tests}, panel~A) Contrast~1 is positive in all five folds ($+0.0046$, 95\% CI $[+0.0022, +0.0076]$; $p_{t} = 0.0415$, $p_{\mathrm{NB}} = 0.1196$, $q_{\mathrm{BH}}^{\mathrm{NB}} = 0.2631$), and its mean is 47.6\% smaller than on frozen features ($+0.0087$), so the point estimates meet neither condition of the rule.

The fold-paired change of the contrast, LoRA minus frozen, is $-0.0041$ (95\% CI $[-0.0078, -0.0004]$; $p_{t} = 0.1236$, $p_{\mathrm{NB}} = 0.2644$, $p_{W} = 0.1875$); a reduction by exactly half corresponds to a change of $-0.0043$, which lies inside this interval, while zero lies outside it; the corresponding Nadeau--Bengio interval $[-0.0130, +0.0047]$ contains both values.

Over the planned family of eleven LoRA-UNI contrasts, none reaches $q_{\mathrm{BH}}^{\mathrm{NB}} < 0.05$ (smallest 0.0805), while with the naive test two reach $q_{\mathrm{BH}} < 0.05$ (\texttt{SpatialMult} versus \texttt{DualBranch} under both hyperparameter sets); none of the six per-configuration LoRA-minus-frozen differences has $p_{\mathrm{NB}} < 0.05$ (smallest 0.0726, \texttt{RetNet}), and the headline-QWK rule of \ref{app:lora_decision} is defined on the five-fold mean alone and is not changed by these tests.
